Compute a diversity coefficient

Source: R/divCoef.R
divCoef.Rd

Computes a quadratic diversity coefficient for each column of a data frame, optionally using a provided distance matrix.

divCoef(df, dis = NULL, normalize = FALSE, tol = 0.00000001)

Arguments

df

a data frame or matrix of non-negative values (e.g. abundances). Rows correspond to entities, columns to samples.

dis

optional object of class dist. If NULL, a default Euclidean distance is used.

normalize

logical; if TRUE, the diversity is scaled by its theoretical maximum

tol

numeric tolerance used for numerical checks

Value

a numeric vector of diversity coefficients, one per column

Details

The diversity coefficient is defined as $$D = \frac{x^T D^2 x}{2 (\sum x)^2}$$ where \(x\) is a column of df and \(D\) is the distance matrix.

If normalize = TRUE, values are divided by the maximum achievable diversity under the given distance matrix.

See also

Other assoc.nominal: contCoef(), cramerV(), entropy(), lambda(), mutInf(), phi(), tschuprowT(), uncertCoef(), yule

Examples

set.seed(1)
df <- matrix(runif(20), ncol = 4)
d <- dist(matrix(rnorm(10), ncol = 2))

divCoef(df, d)
#> [1] 2.095912 1.959129 1.740829 1.485362
divCoef(df, d, normalize = TRUE)
#> [1] 0.8327579 0.7784104 0.6916744 0.5901710
